label: the University of California application

fee.note: Per campus, for international and non-immigrant applicants; 80 USD per campus for domestic applicants. All nine campuses is 855 USD.

rounds.label: University of California application
rounds.note: One thirty-day window and nothing else. No Early Decision, no Early Action, no rolling consideration, no late round, no equivalent of Clearing. The application can be worked on from 1 August but is only accepted between 1 and 30 November 2026, and decisions come back across March 2027. A student who treats 1 January as "the American deadline" has missed all nine University of California campuses by five weeks.

milestones.label: UC application opens for fall 2027
milestones.note: You can start working on the application from 1 August 2026, three months before you may file it.

milestones.label: UC admission decisions for fall 2027
milestones.note: Notification runs through March 2027. Some campuses release earlier.

milestones.label: Statement of Intent to Register (SIR)
milestones.note: How you accept a UC place, and it goes to one campus only. Same day as the national reply date used by the Common App colleges, so a student holding offers on both routes decides everything at once.

milestones.label: Final official transcript to the campus
milestones.note: For students intending to enrol in fall 2027. Postmarked or submitted electronically by this date.

milestones.label: Official IB examination results to UC
milestones.note: This is UC's answer to the July problem, and it is a better answer than most systems in this dataset manage. The IB publishes results on 6 July; UC wants the official results by 15 July. Nine days. Request the transmission from the IB as soon as you have accepted a place, not when the results appear.

submissionItems.label: The UC application, with the academic record self-reported inside it
submissionItems.note: You type your own subjects and grades in. No transcript is sent at application stage; it follows only if you enrol.

submissionItems.label: Four personal insight questions, 350 words each
submissionItems.note: Four short answers chosen from eight prompts, not one long personal essay. A Common App essay does not transfer into this and cannot simply be cut down.

submissionItems.label: Application fee, per campus
submissionItems.note: 95 USD per campus for an international or non-immigrant applicant, 80 USD domestic.

submissionItems.label: No letters of recommendation
submissionItems.destinationOfItem: Nowhere — this step does not exist here
submissionItems.note: Recorded as an item precisely because it is absent. UC states that it does not require, and does not read, letters of recommendation at the time of application; a campus may ask later as part of a supplemental review. A student who spends October chasing references for Berkeley has spent October on the wrong thing.

submissionItems.label: Official IB results, if you enrol
submissionItems.note: Sent by the IB. These are also what the credit award is calculated from: 6 quarter units for a diploma at 30 points or above, and 8 quarter units per Higher Level exam graded 5, 6 or 7.

supplementarySteps: UC Berkeley is the campus in this profile, but the application is the same for all nine and adding campuses costs only the fee. Davis, Irvine, Merced, Riverside, Santa Barbara and Santa Cruz are also the six that run the Transfer Admission Guarantee, which matters to anyone considering the community-college route later.
A Danish student pays nonresident tuition at UC for all four years. Residency for tuition is not something an F-1 student acquires by living in California.
Every registered Berkeley student, international students included, is enrolled automatically in the Berkeley student health plan unless they waive it with proof of comparable cover.

notes: Every date on this route is published by UC against the words "fall 2027", so none of them is inferred and none is provisional.

Not established: whether an international applicant faces any additional documentary requirement inside the UC application, and how a campus treats an offer where the final IB results fall below the predictions.
